title: The 45-minute LLD interview
idea: A low-level design (LLD) interview is a timed conversation: you turn a vague problem into a few well-named classes, code the core path, then show it can grow.
points: Spend the first minutes asking questions and writing down the agreed scope.
List entities and their jobs before you draw any class diagram.
Code one core use case end to end, not every class half done.
Close by adding a requirement through a new class, not by editing old ones.

items.label: Clarify
items.text: Ask who uses it, the main actions and what is out of scope.

items.label: Entities
items.text: Pull nouns from the scope. Give each candidate class one sentence describing its job.

items.label: Diagram
items.text: Sketch a class diagram: fields, key methods, has-a and is-a links.

items.label: Core code
items.text: Write the main use case in runnable classes. Talk while you type.

items.label: Extend
items.text: The interviewer adds a twist. Show where a new class plugs in.

items.label: Wrap up
items.text: Name trade-offs, edge cases you skipped and how you would test them.

code.title: Interview-sized core
code.caption: One practice problem, an expense splitter, cut to its core. Others to try: parking lot, elevator, library. Add a `PercentSplit` class and pass it in. Real money needs integer cents and a rule for the leftover cent; mention it as a trade-off.

walk.text: One strategy class. Its only job is deciding each person's share.
`Expense` holds a strategy in a private field, injected through the constructor.
`split` delegates the rule, so a new rule never edits `Expense`.
The demo: show the interviewer the core path actually runs.

pitfalls: Do not start coding before you and the interviewer agree on scope.
Avoid drawing ten classes; three to five well-named ones show more judgement.
Say your trade-offs out loud; silent good design earns less credit.

quiz.code:
const s = { shares: (amt, ppl) => ppl.map((x) => [x, amt / ppl.length]) };
console.log(Object.fromEntries(s.shares(10, ['ana', 'raj'])));
quiz.why: `shares` returns key-value pairs, each person with 10 divided by 2. `Object.fromEntries` turns those pairs into an object.

takeaway: Clarify, model, code the core, then extend without editing old classes.

starters: Which practice problems should I do first for LLD interviews?
What questions should I ask in the first five minutes?
How do I recover if I run out of time mid-design?
